I have to wonder ... if players are careful enough with their characters (and attempt to either improvise or prepare for different eventualities), I doubt parties die off that quickly (fleeing or 'not going in' is sometimes the smartest option).

When you're doing tabletop luck plays a very big part in a session. 3 bad rolls in a row can lead to a character dying and when one goes down the rest or the party will be in trouble, if they're in a tough spot.

As said in the article most of the cheating done in tabletop is dungeons masters pretending some of his behind-the-screen rolls were not as bad as they should have been. If you're gonna play perfectly fair then you may end up killing your daughter at a convention game, even if it's the least thing you'd want to have happened.

I think dice rolling (there's a technique to influence rolling - apart from loaded dice - that craps players use), and the larger dice (D8, 10, 12 and 20) can sometimes be made to roll certain ways (if a die's edge is not crisp, that's also an influencing factor).

Some P&P games opt for "dicelessness" (which is an option to the myriad D20 fan-adapted rules); I prefer the CoC direct skill percentile and D100 (or two D10s). Seems simpler in my mind anyway.
